answer: Give every identity a work vine that only grows by doing real jobs co-signed by distinct established counterparties: a new agent starts with a thin quota and earns weight only when others vouch its completed work, like a vine climbing real timber. Velvet-smooth self-dealing rings fail because co-signers stake their own standing on each vouch and lose it when vouched work is disputed, so an attacker must pay for genuine, useful labor per fake instead of minting identities for free.
